candidates.title: An overview of magneto-inertial fusion on the Z machine at Sandia National Laboratories (Nuclear Fusion 2022)
candidates.notes: Open-access peer-reviewed article. Contains quantitative plasma parameters at stagnation: ion temps 3.1 keV, peak DD neutron yield 1.1×10¹³, axial field 10–20 T pre-compressed to >1000 T, drive current up to 20 MA, laser preheat 0.5–1.2 kJ. Scaling projections to 60+ MA for high-gain D-T. Directly relevant as D-T framework for D-D scaling.

gaps_attempted.notes: MagLIF D-T experimental data provides the best available analogue for scaling to NearStar's D-D geometry. Key data: 20 MA → DT-equivalent 2 kJ; 60+ MA → high-gain simulations (yield/input > 1000). D-D scaling requires substantially higher drive energy (~100× cross-section disadvantage), placing NearStar's required gain in context. This does not fully resolve the gap (no D-D specific experiment exists) but provides a physics framework.

gaps_attempted.notes: IFE target cost data extracted. Key figures: mass-production cost target $0.17–0.35/target (factory models); NIF-class research targets ~$2,500 each; requirement ~500K–1M targets/day at ≤$0.50. NearStar's 28M shots/year (1 Hz) is ~3× lower than typical IFE plant assumptions. These are D-T ICF targets; NearStar's 50 g D-D magnetized capsule is structurally different and likely more complex, making IFE costs a lower bound rather than a direct estimate.

summary.interpretation_note: This analysis has no gaps typed 'not-yet-sourced' — all gaps are typed 'truly-unknown', 'proprietary', or 'derivable'. Gaps G-3, G-4, G-5, G-7 were treated as functionally researchable because their source recommendations explicitly reference accessible analogue literature. Gaps G-1, G-2 (fusion gain, net electrical output) are genuinely 'truly-unknown' with no accessible source and were skipped. Gaps G-6, G-9–G-15 were not attempted due to search/extraction budget limits; G-8 search was run but extraction skipped.
